title: Cover three steam-table pans, two with ladles in them
instruction: Cover every pan on the steam table to keep the food hot until the next rush.
context: Covering hot-held pans on a steam table between rushes is routine for restaurant cooks (1.4M US workers), food preparation workers (0.9M) and fast food cooks (0.6M); O*NET core tasks include 'complete orders from steam tables' (short order cooks) and 'place food trays over food warmers for immediate service' (food preparation workers). Serving ladles stay in their pans during service, so ladle pans take a notched cover with the handle out through the notch. The instruction doesn't say which cover goes where; taking a ladle out counts as wrong.
setup: Table-top layout, x forward from the line through the two arm bases (61 cm apart), y to the left of the midline. A stainless steam-table section (34 x 55 cm, 2 mm base plate with a 4 mm stainless surround 10.2 cm high) sits centred 30 cm out, on the midline (the pans' rims are 10.2 cm above the table). In it, three 1/3-size stainless hotel pans side by side (each 32.5 x 17.6 cm flange to flange, long side toward the robot, 10 cm deep, thin stainless walls modelled 3 mm thick, 1 cm flange), centred at y = +17.8 cm (left), 0 (middle) and -17.8 cm (right), each with 4.5 cm of food (rice, mixed vegetables, brown sauce). The left and right pans each hold a stainless serving ladle (round bowl 7 cm across, 3 cm deep; 30 cm x 1.8 cm x 0.8 cm flat handle, 0.15 kg), its bowl on the food 3 cm beyond the pan's centre and its handle leaning on the far rim at about 15 degrees and pointing away from the robot; the middle pan has no ladle. Three stainless 1/3-size covers (32.5 x 17.6 cm, 3 mm modelled plate (a real cover is about 0.7 mm sheet with a rolled rim; the sim plate is thicker for stable contact but carries the real mass), 0.35 kg solid and 0.33 kg notched, strap handle on top: 10 x 2 cm bar on two 1.6 cm posts, bar along the cover's short side) lie flat on the table, long sides toward the robot, centred 30 cm out; the covers are plain stainless and look pale grey in the screenshot: a solid cover at y = +37 cm, a notched cover at y = +55.4 cm and a notched cover at y = -37 cm. Each notched cover has a 6 cm deep, 5 cm wide notch cut into its short end nearest the robot. The arms start in their folded ready pose.
scoring: Each pan is worth one third. A pan scores when a cover rests flat on its rim: the cover's underside within 3 mm of the rim top (10.2 cm above the table), its centre within 1.5 cm of the pan's centre, within 3 degrees of level and 5 degrees of square with the pan. A pan with a ladle scores 1/3 for any cover that rests flat (only a notched cover, notch round the handle, can; a solid cover or a notch the wrong way sits about 12 mm proud on the handle and scores 0), provided that ladle has never moved 3 cm or more or turned 10 degrees or more since the start. The empty middle pan scores 1/3 for a solid cover and 1/6 for a notched one (it leaves a gap for heat to escape). A ladle taken out or pushed into the food scores 0 for its pan for the rest of the trial, even if put back. The score counts only at the end, with all covers and ladles moving less than 3 mm over the last second and no gripper finger or fingertip-midpoint within 3 cm of any cover's plate, posts or strap (so a cover held or touched anywhere, including at its edge, is not released); otherwise 0. A cover's centre is the centre of its full plate, measured from a marker at the plate centre, not from the notched cover's off-centre body origin. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Put the ladles back with bowls on the food and handles on the far rim, and the covers back in their starting places. In real trials the pans hold dry rice, dry beans and lentils (unheated).
fidelity: Full size; no heat or steam. Pans are rigid thin-walled boxes fixed in the table; food is a solid layer; the ladle bowl is a solid disc. Covers are 3 mm plates (real: about 0.7 mm sheet) at the real mass, 0.35 kg (0.33 notched), for stable contact; strap handle on posts. Spill and heat are not modelled; choosing the cover, orienting the notch and seating it flat are.
